subject: Food Science
title: Margarine vs. Butter Wars
description: A quick win: understand Margarine vs. Butter Wars.

hook.text: In 1886, five US states banned margarine outright. Others required it to be dyed pink so consumers wouldn't mistake it for butter.

buildup.text: Hippolyte Mège-Mouriès invented margarine in 1869 to win a Napoleon III prize—a cheap butter substitute for soldiers and the poor.

discovery.text: Margarine was made from beef tallow and milk. Hydrogenation (1901) allowed plant oils—cheaper and more shelf-stable.

twist.text: The dairy lobby fought margarine for 80 years with bans, taxes, and color restrictions.

climax.text: The irony: trans fats from hydrogenated margarine turned out to be far worse for heart health than the butter it replaced.

punchline.text: Made to replace butter. Banned to protect dairy. Then proven worse than what it replaced.

quiz.question: Why were some US states forcing margarine to be dyed pink?
options: So consumers wouldn't mistake it for butter—dairy lobby-backed regulation
It was a food safety requirement
